DDR4-2666 holds its rated speed at two DIMMs per channel -- it is the grade vendors recommend precisely because it does not derate. Dell's Cascade Lake genomics study recommends 2DPC DDR4-2666 over 1DPC DDR4-2933 for that reason: the extra channel population beats the higher clock.

DDR4-2933 is confirmed as a real Ice Lake-SP grade: the cited page's Platinum SKU table lists "8xDDR4-2933" for 8351N and 8352V. At one DIMM per channel the grade runs at its rated speed, which is what effective_mts records here.

DDR4-2933 is confirmed as a real Ice Lake-SP grade: the cited page's Platinum SKU table lists "8xDDR4-2933" for 8351N and 8352V. At one DIMM per channel the grade runs at its rated speed, which is what effective_mts records here.

Capacity variant of the same grade. Module capacity does not change the clock at a given DIMM-per-channel count -- speed is a property of the DDR grade and the population, which is what the cited source states and what effective_mts records. 16 GB RDIMMs are a standard server SKU and are the cheapest way to populate every channel on an 8- or 12-channel board, which is what actually determines bandwidth. Rank count (1Rx8 vs 2Rx8) is not modelled: it can matter at 2 DIMMs per channel, so treat 2DPC figures for this capacity as the same first-order estimate as the rest of the table.

Capacity variant of the same grade; see the 16 GB row for why capacity does not change the clock. 8 GB RDIMMs are the floor for filling every channel cheaply -- eight of them fill an 8-channel board for 64 GB, which is enough for a 7B model at Q4 and gives full bandwidth. They are single-rank, so bank parallelism is lower than a 2-rank module of the same grade; that effect is not modelled here and would make these slightly optimistic.

Cascade Lake and Ice Lake both list DDR4-2933 as a platform grade. It is recorded here as holding at 2DPC, which is the optimistic reading: some vendor tables drop 2933 to 2666 at 2DPC on 1st/2nd gen boards. Treated as a known upper bound rather than a measured floor -- see the notes on this row before quoting a 2DPC DDR4-2933 build.
